safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting the absence of unwell contacts has minimal impact on immediate management for an uncomplicated respiratory illness and mainly affects epidemiologic/contextual detail. Core symptomatic review (no N/V) was still captured.

safety_verdicts.content: Subjective fevers, chills, and night sweats

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Recording 'subjective fevers' when fever was not established can bias diagnostic thinking toward influenza/bacterial infection and may prompt unnecessary monitoring, testing, or antibiotic use. The patient did report hot/cold and sweating, so the discrepancy is unlikely to drastically change care but can still mislead.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Contradicts gold (blocked ears present) and transcript (patient answers 'yeah' to dullness/blocked ears), so 'no ear pain or blockage' is incorrect.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting no ear blockage when the patient endorsed blocked ears can lead to under-assessment of ear complications (e.g., otitis media, eustachian tube dysfunction) and missed symptomatic treatment. Typically this results in discomfort/persistent symptoms rather than major harm.
